When a policy file is clearing a key, all values and markers under the key are dropped and a single clear-all marker is stored. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:183)
When a key's clearance is forgotten in a policy file, every clear-all marker for that key is removed. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:190)

The registry values a policy touches are its own value, those in its value lists, those of its elements (the whole key for list elements) and those of checkbox and choice sub-lists, each counted once. (PolicyPlus/PolicyProcessing.vb:213)

A policy's lists of on-values and off-values count as enabled or disabled evidence for each value in them that is present, using the list's own key when it names one. (PolicyPlus/PolicyProcessing.vb:11)

For a checkbox element: a value marked for deletion counts as one deleted element. Otherwise, each present off value (or off-list value) counts a tenth of a deleted element, and each present on value (or on-list value) counts one present element. A checkbox whose template declares no on value or on list adds no present evidence, even if it holds 1. (PolicyPlus/PolicyProcessing.vb:50)
A semantic policy script is refused unless its first line is 'Policy Plus Semantic Policy', with the message 'Incorrect signature.'. (PolicyPlus/SpolFile.vb:50)

A policy header line in a semantic policy script is a user policy only when its first word is exactly 'U'. Any other first word, including lowercase 'u' or 'User', is a machine policy. rules: A category is orphaned when it has no parent among the loaded definitions although its definition names one. (PolicyPlus/Main.vb:171)

When a policy file is clearing a key, all values and markers under the key are dropped and a single clear-all marker is stored. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:183)
A category is visible when empty categories are switched on. Otherwise it is visible only if it has at least one visible policy or one visible subcategory. (PolicyPlus/Main.vb:196)

A policy is visible only if it applies to a chosen area (user, computer or both). With "Only Filtered Policies" on, it must also pass the filter for a chosen area it applies to; passing for either one is enough. (PolicyPlus/Main.vb:204)
